newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Buthelezi rejects ANC truth submission.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Buthelezi rejects ANC truth submission.

text.p: South Africa's main black opposition leader Mangosuthu Buthelezi on Wednesday rejected assertions by the ruling African National Congress that it had never regarded him as a military target.

Buthelezi, leader of the Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party, was responding to ANC statements to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in which it admitted that some members had once suggested killing Buthelezi.

But the ANC said it had never fought Inkatha, only agents of the white government which it said had tried to foment hostility between the two groups. About 15,000 people died in a decade of feuding between ANC and Inkatha.
Deputy President Thabo Mbeki said earlier the ANC leadership had vetoed suggestions from some units that Buthelezi be killed and that a public building used by Inkatha be blown up.
Buthelezi said in a statement he welcomed Mbeki's admission of the assassination plot, which he said the ANC had previously stubbornly denied.

"One wonders how to assess the other denials made by the ANC with respect to the many allegations that for two decades they...used violence and intimidation as tools of political action to gain support within black constituencies," Buthelezi said.
He repeated a charge he has frequently made before that the ANC or its allies had killed more than 420 Inkatha leaders.
"These serial killings represent a crime against humanity... I cannot accept the assertion that Inkatha was never an ANC military target," Buthelezi said.

He said Inkatha had sent the truth commission "a large volume of evidence" to show that the ANC had singled out his party as a collaborator and enemy of the people -- "buzz words to identify targets of military actions".
Buthelezi said senior ANC leaders had publicly called for the murder of Inkatha office-bearers.
"There will never be lasting reconciliation between the ANC and my party unless based on truth and acceptance of culpability for the murder of our leaders," he said.
Buthelezi, whose party has majority support in KwaZulu-Natal province, serves as home affairs minister in the government of national unity.
He is acting president of the country during the absence of Nelson Mandela and Mbeki, who are hoping to host Zairean peace talks on a South African navy ship off Congo.
